subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class cron-scoped tool policy such as `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny`, make cron inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or handle the `message` tool only through delivery-mode defaults?
rationale: This changes a public config and tool-execution boundary for scheduled jobs, and automation cannot safely choose the permanent precedence or security model.

options.title: Add explicit cron policy
options.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence against existing tool-policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat isolated cron sessions as inheriting `tools.subagents.tools`, reducing new config surface but coupling two different execution modes.

options.title: Message-only safeguard
options.body: Only harden announce delivery around direct `message` use, which addresses the duplicate-message symptom but leaves broader cron tool restriction unsolved.

recommendation.title: Add explicit cron policy
recommendation.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence against existing tool-policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current blame and prior-review signal across the cron delivery and tool-policy surfaces.
